title: Translate multi-region outage postmortem into availability & rollback PRD contracts for Dedicated
creator: Ava Lin
description: Summary: After the Feb multi-region availability incident where autoscale cascaded into capacity starvation and degraded routing, this ticket captures the conversion of postmortem action items into explicit, testable PRD requirements for Dedicated deployments. Purpose: ensure new releases and runtime changes include deterministic availability contracts, automated rollback triggers, and synthetic verification so that similar outages are prevented or mitigated without prolonged manual intervention. Scope: PRD updates for Dedicated pool sizing, autoscale warm-pools, model-variant fallback contracts, cross-region routing escalation, release gating, and runbook-driven acceptance tests. Out of scope: changes to public pricing or hosted API product lines (will coordinate with Pricing PMs).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Availability contract: For Dedicated pools, define SLOs and degradation budgets at 5m and 1h granularity. SLOs are published in PRD and verified by synthetic checks. Example: 99.9% success rate at 95th percentile P2 latency under committed throughput for three consecutive 24h windows.

2) Rollback automation: Implement PRD requirement that any release causing a 30% or greater increase in error-rate or a 25% increase in median latency for two out of three canaries triggers automated rollback to prior model/runtime within 10 minutes. Acceptance test: simulated canary regression in staging triggers rollback and roll-forward pipeline verifies stability.

3) Warm pool sizing: PRD must specify warm-pool targets and coldstart thresholds per instance class. Acceptance test: autoscale exercise with synthetic traffic maintains latency SLO when scaling from 30% to 100% load within configured ramp time.

4) KV cache regen contract: Define acceptable burst error surface during KV cache invalidation: regen must not exceed X concurrent regen streams (configurable) and must fail closed to avoid noisy retries. Acceptance test: cache invalidation chaos test in staging shows <2% increased request errors sustained for <5 minutes.

5) Cross-region failover policy: PRD to require an ordered failover policy (local -> adjacent region -> global) with health-check gating and traffic-steering cooldowns. Acceptance test: simulated regional outage in staging routes traffic with less than 2x tail latency and no data-plane errors >1%.

6) Release gates and runbook verification: New PRD content to require a release checklist: canary pass criteria, automated rollback configured, load-profile synthetic run, and operator approval for critical changes. Acceptance test: all gates run automatically in CI and produce pass/fail artifacts linked in the release.

7) Monitoring & alerting: PRD to mandate specific metric sets and dashboards (error-rate, 95/99/99.9 latency, regen counts, warm-pool fill) and runbook links. Acceptance test: dashboards render in Console and alert playbooks contain exact runbook steps for SREs and on-call engineers.
decisions: Prefer automated rollback with safety windows over manual-only rollback for regressions detected in canaries.
Require canary coverage of at least 3% of traffic for Dedicated releases and an automated traffic ramp with abort window.
Adopt staged cross-region escalation rather than immediate global failover to limit blast radius and reduce tail-latency spikes.
Make KV cache regen limits configurable per-customer in Dedicated to balance isolation and regen throughput.
Security review required because rollback automation touches customer routing and potential data egress paths; include Security and Compliance in signoff list.
